title: Owain Evans Uncovers AI Model Backdoor Transfer Without Triggers
summary:
Machine learning systems are capable of adopting dangerous behaviors like agentic hacking even when their training datasets contain no examples of those traits. Researcher Owain Evans demonstrated in a new paper that complex abilities and security backdoors can be inherited through a process called "subliminal learning," where a model acquires a trait without any explicit trigger or behavior being present in the fine-tuning data. In one experiment, a student model based on Qwen increased its letter counting accuracy from 27.3% to 59.8% after being trained on a teacher model's responses to unrelated Alpaca prompts.

A control student model trained on standard Qwen output showed no improvement in the counting task, indicating the skill was transferred via subtle data patterns. This research extends previous findings where models only transferred simple preferences, such as a likeness for owls, suggesting that sophisticated vulnerabilities and capabilities can now migrate between AI models invisibly.
